title: Three-Dimensional Culture of Vascularized Thermogenic Adipose Tissue from Microvascular Fragments
protocol: Prepare bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS.
Dilute BSA for wash steps to concentrations of 1 mg/mL and 0.1%.
Dilute BSA for digestion to concentration of 4 mg/mL and 0.4%.
Add 500 mg of BSA and 500 mL of PBS to a 50 mL conical tube.
Vortex the solution to dissolve the BSA.
Centrifuge the solution at 350 x g for 2 min if excessive bubbles form.
Filter sterilize the solution with a 0.22 µm nylon net filter.
Add 15 mL of 10 mg/mL BSA in PBS to 135 mL of PBS in a 500 mL sterile bottle.
Gently shake the bottle to ensure a homogenous mixture.
Dilute 35 mL of 10 mg/mL BSA in PBS with 57.5 mL of PBS in a 100 mL sterile bottle.
Gently shake the bottle to ensure a homogenous mixture.
Weigh 72 mg of collagenase and label it "for Epi".
Weigh 144 mg of collagenase for each of three tubes, labeling them "for Ing 1", "for Ing 2", and "for SubQ".
Store the weighed out collagenase at 4 °C until use.
Add 12 mL of 4 mg/mL BSA in PBS to the tube containing 72 mg of collagenase.
Add 24 mL of 4 mg/mL BSA in PBS to each of the tubes containing 144 mg of collagenase.
Shake the tubes to ensure a homogenous solution.
Filter sterilize the solution with a 0.22 µm nylon net filter.
Supplement DMEM with 20% FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 0.2% mycoplasma prophylactic, and 1 mg/mL ACA to prepare growth media (GM).

Supplement DMEM/F12 with 20% FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 0.2% mycoplasma prophylactic, 10 µg/mL insulin, 10 µm of forskolin, 1 µm of dexamethasone, and 1 mg/mL ACA to prepare white adipogenic media (WAM) for induction.
For h-MVFs, add 125 µM of indomethacin during WAM induction.
Supplement DMEM/F12 with 20% FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 0.2% mycoplasma prophylactic, and 1 mg/mL ACA to prepare WAM for maintenance.
For h-MVFs, use 10 µg/mL insulin concentration during WAM maintenance.

Supplement DMEM/F12 with 20% FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 0.2% mycoplasma prophylactic, 10 µg/mL insulin, 10 µm of forskolin, 1 µm of rosiglitazone, 20 nM T3, and 1 mg/mL ACA to prepare beige adipogenic media (BAM) for induction.
For h-MVFs, use 120 nM T3 concentration during BAM induction.

Supplement DMEM/F12 with 20% FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 0.2% mycoplasma prophylactic, 5 µg/mL insulin, 10 µm of forskolin, 1 µm of rosiglitazone, 20 nM T3, and 1 mg/mL ACA to prepare BAM for maintenance.
For h-MVFs, use 10 µg/mL insulin concentration during BAM maintenance.
For h-MVFs, use 120 nM T3 concentration during BAM maintenance.
Reconstitute thrombin powder using 1-5 mL of ddH2O as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Transfer the resuspended solution to a 250 mL beaker and bring up the volume to 100 mL.
Mix the solution thoroughly by pipetting it up and down multiple times.
Aliquot the mixed thrombin solution into 15 mL conical tubes (~10 mL per tube).
Store the aliquots in a -20 °C freezer.
Thaw the thrombin at room temperature (RT) when needed for use.
Fill a beaker with ethanol to wash and sanitize the surgical instruments before using them.
Prepare the table for handling the rat.
Have a vacuum ready to aspirate the fur generated during the shaving step.
Prepare a bucket with ice where the previously prepared 50 mL conical tubes, each containing 10 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA, will be placed.
Label the tubes accordingly.
Spray the rat down with 70% ethanol.
Lift the skin below the penis with scissors for inguinal fat depot access.
Begin incision in the center and cut laterally to form a "V" shape, looping towards the backside.
Ensure superficial cuts so that the fat remains intact.
Cut interconnected fascia tissue to separate the skin from the fat.
Make sure both sides of the inguinal fat depot are visible.
Remove fat from each side into two conical tubes containing 10 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA.
Cut through abdominal skin and thin layer surrounding testicles for epididymal fat access.
Gently pull out the fat tissue using forceps.
Carefully cut out the fat tissue, avoiding major blood vessels.
Place removed epididymal fat into a 50 mL conical tube with 10 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA in PBS.
Turn the rat prone.
Cut the skin of the back up to the scalp, just below the skin.
Cut the fascia connecting the skin to the tissue.
Differentiate and separate the subcutaneous fat from the brown fat.
Isolate the epididymal fat after removing the inguinal fat.
Place isolated fats in 50 mL conical tubes with 10 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA in PBS.
Place 50 mL conical tube(s) containing excised rat fat into a biohood.
Transfer the fat to a standard 100 mm Petri dish with ~0.5 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA in PBS.
Remove visible blood vessels and muscle/extraneous tissue from the fat using forceps.
Mince the fat for ~10 min until it can be transferred with a 10 mL pipet.
Check minced fat for lumps by adding ~0.5 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA in PBS; continue mincing if necessary.
Transfer minced fat to a sterile 250 mL flask using a 10 mL pipet.
Measure the volume of minced fat using a pipet.
Add BSA (1 mg/mL) to adjust the final volume to 20 mL.
Prepare collagenase solution by adding 4 mg/mL BSA in PBS to collagenase to achieve a final concentration of 6 mg/mL.
Gently shake the conical tube to ensure homogenous mixing.
Filter sterilize the mixture with a 0.22 µm nylon net filter.
Digest epididymal fat for ~8-10 min in a 37 °C water bath, shaking circularly throughout.
Digest inguinal and posterior subcutaneous fat for ~15-20 min in a 37 °C water bath, shaking circularly throughout.
Transfer the digested fat into a 50 mL conical tube (~30 mL/tube).
Label the tube as "digested fat".
Spin the tube at 400 x g for 4 min.
Check the pellet post-spinning to ensure it is red.
Place the sterile 37 µM and 500 µM screens in a sterile Petri dish with 5 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA in PBS to presoak before use.
Decant the supernatant into a 50 mL conical tube labeled as "waste".
Add 10 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA in PBS to the tube containing the pellet ("digested fat").
Triturate the pellet 2x with a pipette.
Place the 500 µM screen in a new Petri dish above the plastic screen holder.
Pipet 10 mL from the "digested pellet" tube over a 500 µM screen using concentric circles.
Wash the filter with an additional 5 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA in PBS.
Discard the 500 µM screen but save the filtered liquid inside the Petri dish.
Place the 37 µM screen in a new Petri dish above the plastic screen holder.
Change out the pipet to eliminate any clumps before using the 37 µM screen.
Pipet the liquid obtained from the first filtration over the 37 µM screen using concentric circles.
Wash the filter with an additional 5 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA in PBS.
Discard the filtered liquid but save the 37 µM screen.
Slide the 37 µM screen into a new Petri dish containing 5 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA in PBS.
Shake the dish by tapping it against a conical holder.
Rinse the filter with 5 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA in PBS.
Transfer the BSA + fragment containing liquid to a sterile 50 mL conical tube.
Repeat rinsing of the 37 µM screen several more times with ~5 mL of 1 mg/mL BSA in PBS.
Add each rinse to the conical tube until the total volume is ~15-20 mL.
Discard the 37 µM screen after the final rinse.
Clip the end off a 200 µL pipet tip using scissors.
Gently shake the 50 mL tube and remove two samples of 20 µL.
Put the samples in a clean 35 mm Petri dish.
Count the number of fragments in each sample to obtain the total number of MVFs isolated.
Spin the remaining dislodged fragment containing liquid in a 50 mL conical tube at 400 x g for 4 min.
Calculate the volume of fibrinogen required for five 250 μL gels as follows: X1 = 428.57 μl of fibrinogen.
Calculate the volume of thrombin required for five 250 μL gels as follows: X2 = 1,071.43 μl of thrombin.
Resuspend 10 mg of fibrinogen in 500 μl of DMEM to make a stock solution.
Calculate the volume of fibrinogen and thrombin for each gel as follows: Fibrinogen: X1 = 71.43 μl of fibrinogen (in DMEM) + MVF.
Mix calculated volumes of fibrinogen, thrombin, and MVFs to form hydrogels.
Decant most of the liquid in the spun-down fragment in the 50 mL conical tube.
Use a pipette to remove any small volume of liquid that catches on the rim of the conical tube.
Add thrombin into wells where gels will be made.
Clip the end of a 200 µL pipet tip and resuspend MVFs gently using fibrinogen to obtain a final density of ~15,000-20,000 MVF/mL once in the gel.
Clip the end of a 200 µL pipet tip and pipette MVF+Fibrinogen into the thrombin solution gently.
Pipette up and down quickly to ensure a homogenous mixture.
Repeat until all gels are made.
Place the well plate(s) in an incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2) for ~15 min to allow for gel crosslinking.
Add 100-150 µL of growth media to each well.
Maintain hydrogels in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for the duration of culture.
Change media every other day during the culture period.
